intent: Fix the Bokeh DatePicker showing the selected day minus one for browsers in UTC+ timezones (issue #9129) by having DatePickerView._unlocal_date subtract the browser's timezone offset before taking the ISO calendar date it hands to Pikaday. Adds the widget's first Selenium integration tests (label render, JS on_change + displayed text, server round trip). Must show the user-specified calendar day in every browser timezone (UTC+, UTC, UTC-) for value, min_date and max_date, without regressing the value sent back to Python.

findings.title: UTC- browsers now show Python-supplied dates one day early
findings.suggested_fix: Stop shifting the timestamp unconditionally; choose the calendar-day reading by representation. Pass the raw model value to the helper: for the toDateString() string that _on_select stores (parsed by new Date() as local time) return new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate()); for everything else (milliseconds from Python, or an ISO YYYY-MM-DD string, both UTC) return new Date(d.getUTCFullYear(), d.getUTCMonth(), d.getUTCDate()). Assumption: the only local-time strings reaching the view are the ones _on_select writes and the model default new Date().toDateString(). A scratch node run of this branch gave the intended day for millisecond, time-of-day, picked-string and ISO inputs in UTC, Europe/Paris, Europe/London, Asia/Kolkata, Pacific/Auckland, America/New_York, America/Los_Angeles, America/Sao_Paulo and Pacific/Honolulu.
findings.why_it_matters: Every user west of UTC (all of the Americas) now sees the initial value, min_date and max_date one calendar day early: DatePicker(value=date(2019, 9, 20)) renders 'Thu Sep 19 2019' in New York or Los Angeles, and min_date=date(2019, 9, 1) becomes Aug 31. The base code showed these correctly in every zone. The same shift rolls a value carrying a late-evening UTC time of day (the tests' own max_date=datetime.utcnow()) forward a day for UTC+ users. _unlocal_date receives two representations: UTC-midnight milliseconds from Python, and the local-time toDateString() string _on_select writes. Subtracting the browser offset is right only for the string, so the change fixes issue #9129's after-pick display in UTC+ by breaking first render and bounds in UTC-. Branching on the representation fixes both.
evidence: bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:82-83 -- const timeOffsetInMS = date.getTimezoneOffset() * 60000 / date.setTime(date.getTime() - timeOffsetInMS)
bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:68,70,71 -- defaultDate, minDate and maxDate all pass through this._unlocal_date(new Date(this.model.<prop>)), so all three shift together.

bokeh/util/serialization.py:177-184 -- datetime and date values are serialized as milliseconds since DT_EPOCH with naive values read as UTC, so the number Python sends is already UTC-midnight and needs no offset correction.
bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:95 -- this.model.value = date.toDateString() -- the only local-time representation, and the one issue #9129 is about.

Executed (node, base and head function bodies copied verbatim): input Date.UTC(2019,8,20) -> base 'Fri Sep 20 2019' in every zone; head 'Thu Sep 19 2019' under TZ=America/Los_Angeles and TZ=America/New_York. Input Date.UTC(2019,8,1) -> head 'Sat Aug 31 2019' in both. Input 2019-09-20T23:30Z -> head 'Sat Sep 21 2019' under Europe/Paris, Europe/London, Asia/Kolkata, Pacific/Auckland (base 'Fri Sep 20 2019'). Picked string 'Mon Sep 16 2019' -> head correct in all zones, base 'Sun Sep 15 2019' in the UTC+ zones (the bug being fixed).

Adversarial read, independent sweep of every day 1900-2100 on the Python-milliseconds path: base wrong on 0 days in every zone tested; head wrong on all 67536 days in America/New_York, America/Chicago, America/Los_Angeles, America/Sao_Paulo, America/Havana and America/Santiago.

Follow-on: the stored value is untouched until the user acts, so the wrong day is display-only at first; but with min_date a day early a user can pick and send to Python a date before the configured minimum, and a server-side dp.value = <date> re-renders an already-correct picker through the shifted numeric path (date_picker.ts:54 re-renders on every model change).

findings.title: New tests pass with or without the fix in UTC
findings.suggested_fix: In test_js_on_change_executes, assert the input's value is 'Fri Sep 20 2019' before the first click, then run the display assertions under at least one UTC+ and one UTC- browser timezone. Assumption: the simplest lever is the TZ environment variable of the process that launches the driver in bokeh/_testing/plugins/selenium.py (or Chrome's Emulation.setTimezoneOverride); if neither is acceptable in CI, cover _unlocal_date with a bokehjs unit test run under TZ=America/New_York and TZ=Europe/Paris.
findings.why_it_matters: The new suite cannot tell this change from its absence when the browser runs in UTC, and cannot see finding #1 in any timezone. With a zero offset the two added lines are a no-op, so all three tests give the same result on base and head. The only assertion on displayed text comes after a click, which exercises the picked-string path; the initially rendered date, the thing that breaks west of UTC, is never read. Asserting the initial text and running under one UTC+ and one UTC- zone would make the suite fail for both the original bug and the regression.
evidence: tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py:68 -- assert el.get_attribute('value') == 'Mon Sep 16 2019' -- the only assertion on displayed text, made after clicking day 16 (lines 58-62), so it covers the toDateString() path only.

bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:82 -- const timeOffsetInMS = date.getTimezoneOffset() * 60000 -- evaluates to 0 in a UTC browser, making line 83 a no-op; node under TZ=UTC gives identical base and head output for every input tried.

bokeh/_testing/plugins/selenium.py:61-67 -- the Chrome driver is created with only --headless, --no-sandbox and --window-size; no TZ or timezone setting was found in the testing plugins, .travis.yml or scripts/ci, so the browser inherits the machine's zone.
tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py:96,98 -- the server round-trip test asserts only Python-side values, which come from _on_select and are untouched by this change.

residual_risks: adversarial: picked dates in eras with sub-minute local-mean-time offsets are still shown a day early after this change, because getTimezoneOffset() returns whole minutes (a 1900-2100 sweep of the picked-string path left 3762 wrong days in Europe/Paris before 1911, 2016 in Asia/Kolkata before 1906, 120 in Europe/Dublin in 1916). Matters only for pickers used for historical dates; reading local calendar components instead of shifting the timestamp removes it.

Pikaday is not vendored in the clone and was not inspected, so how it clamps a default date that falls outside the shifted minDate/maxDate was not traced; finding #1's bound consequences are stated at the level of the option values passed in.
Whether the project's CI browser runs in UTC could not be confirmed from the repository; the first half of finding #2 depends on it, the missing assertion on the initially rendered date does not.

Nothing was run against the real widget: the project build, the Selenium suite and a browser were unavailable, so finding #1 rests on the head and base _unlocal_date bodies executed in node under TZ overrides plus the Python serialization source.
testing_gaps: No test covers a server-side assignment (dp.value = date(...) in a Python callback) reaching an already-rendered picker, which switches the client value from the local date string back to UTC milliseconds and re-renders through the other path.
